artboards.title: Sanger vs HTS - what gets sequenced
B - One genome, two branches (not chosen)
C - Same molecule, two rows (not chosen)

annotations.text:
IN THE DECK as slide "Sanger vs. HTS - what gets sequenced" (w1b_omics-data.qmd), exported to img/sanger-vs-hts_panels.png at 2x.

Set in Source Sans Pro - the same face the reveal.js slides use, embedded in this artboard so it matches and needs no network.

Sized so it reads when projected: at 95% slide width the panel headings land around 24px against 30px body text. If you edit the type here, re-export at 1400x750.

OPTION B - one genome, two branches

Not chosen. One genome up top, two routes out of it: makes "same input, different selection" structural rather than implied.

Tradeoff: tallest of the three, a poor fit for a 16:9 slide, and no primers visible - the selection step lives in the arrow labels. Still set in Georgia.

OPTION C - same molecule, two rows

Not chosen, but the closest runner-up: one stretch of DNA drawn twice, intact above and shattered below, in the most slide-friendly shape of the three.

Tradeoff: reads as one molecule rather than a whole genome, and there is no room for a "what comes out" step. Still set in Georgia.
